text: Avalon is the Arthurian Otherworld. The name comes from the word for apple, and the apple is the symbol of the island. Avalon is a beautiful place with mild weather and eternal spring. Flowers and fruit grow on the same trees, and no storm ever rages there. King Arthur ruled Camelot in the mortal world. When he was ready to pass from this world, mysterious women carried him by boat to Avalon. A queen rules the island, sometimes named as Argante. She and her maiden attendants are great healers. A shadowy figure named Avalloc appears as lord of Avalon in some legends. Glastonbury in southwest England is often linked with Avalon today, but this association is post-Celtic. It may derive from the town's ancient name Ynys-witrin, which means glass island. To the Celts, Avalon was one of the western isles of the Otherworld where the dead and the divine mingle.
objective: This article establishes Avalon as the Arthurian Otherworld, a mythical island of apples ruled by a healer queen and a shadowy lord and later linked to Glastonbury.
